name: KAHN SHAKER
desc: The INNOLAB INSTRUMENTS INNO-KHSK-34L Kahn Shaker is a heavy-duty horizontal reciprocating shaker engineered specifically for clinical and pathology laboratories. It is essential for providing smooth, powerful, and consistent back-and-forth agitation to mix samples in Kahn racks during critical serological and flocculation tests.
principle: The Kahn Shaker works on the principle of controlled horizontal reciprocating (linear back-and-forth) motion. A DC motor drives an eccentric cam/crank mechanism that converts rotary motion into a linear to-and-fro stroke of the platform, with the speed (RPM) regulated by varying the DC voltage supplied to the motor and displayed digitally on the panel. The continuous, uniform agitation keeps the reagent-sample mixture in constant motion, which ensures homogeneous mixing without foaming or splashing. In the serology and pathology laboratory this is essential for flocculation tests such as the VDRL (Venereal Disease Research Laboratory) and RPR (Rapid Plasma Reagin) tests for syphilis, where patient serum is mixed with a cardiolipin-lecithin-cholesterol antigen. The cardiolipin antigen forms a colloidal suspension, and when reagin antibodies are present, the antigen particles aggregate into visible flocculates (clumps) that are read microscopically or macroscopically. Gentle, standardized, time-controlled shaking (typically 4 minutes at about 180-200 RPM for VDRL) promotes antigen-antibody collision and lattice formation, so that reproducible and reliable results can be obtained. The same principle is used for the latex agglutination assays (ASO, CRP, RA factor), blood grouping and cross-matching agglutination, and for general mixing of reagents, buffers, serum dilutions and suspensions in test tubes, vials, flasks and bottles held on the rods. Because flocculation and agglutination are sensitive to shaking speed and duration, a calibrated RPM and a timer are critical for the reproducibility of results and for avoiding false-positive or false-negative readings. Since the samples handled are human serum and plasma, which are potentially infectious (HIV, HBV, HCV), the shaker also serves as a bench-top biosafety aid by providing enclosed, hands-free mixing instead of manual rotation of slides or tubes.
sop: Place the Kahn Shaker on a stable, level, vibration-free bench near an earthed 220-230V AC, 50 Hz socket. Keep the area dry and away from reagent spills.
Check that the platform is clear and the adjustable steel rods with rubber sleeves are in place and free of dust or old spills. Wipe with 70% ethanol if required.

Load the Kahn rack, test tubes, vials or flasks onto the platform and adjust the steel rods so that they are held firmly and snugly, without any loose movement. Ensure that all tubes are capped or covered and the load is balanced across the platform.
Connect the power cord to the mains supply, then turn ON the main switch and MCB.
Make sure that the speed regulator knob is at the minimum (zero) position before starting.
Press the 'SET' button to enter the timer setting mode.
Use the 'UP' and 'DOWN' arrows to set the required shaking time (e.g., 4 minutes for the VDRL test; range 0-999 min). Press 'SET' again to lock the timer.

Press the 'START' button and slowly turn the speed regulator knob clockwise to increase the speed until the digital LED display shows the required RPM (e.g., 180-200 RPM for the VDRL/flocculation test).
Wait for stabilization. Allow the RPM reading to settle and observe that the reciprocating motion is smooth, with no spilling or tube movement.
When the set time is over, the shaker will stop automatically. Turn the speed regulator back to zero, remove the rack carefully and read the results immediately as per your test protocol.

After the work, switch OFF the unit, turn OFF the main switch and MCB, and unplug the power cord. Clean the platform and rods with a soft cloth dampened with a mild disinfectant (e.g., 70% ethanol or 0.5% sodium hypochlorite on the metal parts), and wipe dry to avoid corrosion.

SAFETY WARNING: Always treat serum and plasma samples as potentially infectious and wear gloves, a lab coat and safety glasses. Never overload the platform beyond its rated capacity, and never start the shaker at high RPM suddenly. Do not touch or place your hand on the moving platform while running, and never leave the machine unattended with open tubes. Always unplug the mains supply before cleaning or maintenance, and clean up any spills immediately to prevent electrical hazards.
